newsitem.title: MEXICO: Left ahead in Mexico City mayor's race - poll.
newsitem.headline: Left ahead in Mexico City mayor's race - poll.

text.p: Mexico's main leftist party is leading by a big margin in the first election for a mayor of Mexico City, according to a poll published on Wednesday.

The University of Guadalajara's Opinion Studies Centre (CEO) released a survey showing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas more than seven percentage points ahead of his nearest rival, a conservative.

Cardenas, a former president's son who twice ran for president, had 34.8 percent to 27.5 percent for National Action Party (PAN) candidate Carlos Castillo Peraza. President Ernesto Zedillo's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) trailed well behind with 20.5 percent.

The Mexico City mayor's race is one of the most closely watched elections here this year because of the capital's size and political weight. Previously, the mayor was appointed by the president from within the ranks of the PRI.

The survey's findings were broadly in line with those of another poll published on March 10 by Indemerc/Louis Harris, which also put Cardenas ahead. Analysts say the choice of Cardenas boosted the PRD's standing considerably with voters, while the PAN's selection of acerbic former party leader and intellectual Castillo Peraza cost it support.
The CEO survey was carried out on a sample of 800 voters from March 13-14 and had a margin of error of 3.4 percent.

It found that the PRI had a strong negative image, with 54.2 percent of voters saying they would definitely not vote for it. Only 16.8 percent said they would definitely not choose the PRD and 11.12 rejected the PAN.
The main reason cited for refusing to vote PRI was that voters considered the party dishonest, CEO said.
